clues: This city is the second largest in the Mexican state of Michoacán. It sits at the west edge of high lands, east of Tierra Caliente.
Summers here are very wet, while winters stay dry, and green woods thrive. Most of the year's rain falls in the warm summer months.
Friar Juan de San Miguel laid out the new city in 1534. The Spanish had first seized this land twelve years before that year.
In years of war with France, this city served as the capital of its state. It played a big part in an earlier war for freedom too.
This city is the heart of the land's avocado trade. Most of that green crop is sent out from here to the world.
